title: Ship the Lore pane mod in the opum-lore plugin (OPAG-1075)
description:
Operator decision OPAG-1075, relayed by opum-doc as ODOC-OP-2026-10-02-11; operator chose "A: dispatch to lore-cli (Recommended)". lore-cli builds the mod in the opum-lore plugin, releases it, and opum-marketplace moves the pin.

WHAT. A Claude Code hooks module (a "mod") shipped in the opum-lore plugin from this repository: a Lore pane that views documents (raw and rendered markdown), searches, edits and creates. Design brief: opum-doc `docs/reference/lore-mod-design-brief.md`, read by ref at main e62e764 on 2026-10-02. opum-marketplace's opum-lore entry pins opum-ai/lore-cli at v0.12.0 (read by ref 2026-10-02); after this release exists, opum-agent dispatches the pin move.

PLATFORM. Mods need Claude Code 2.1.287 or later; the fleet runs the frozen 2.1.287 pair.

SIBLING. quest-cli's Quest board mod (QCLI-431, draft opum-ai/quest-cli#481) is the pattern mirrored here: plugin-root hooks/, types/, tests/; scripts/mod-test.mjs stages exactly the shipped files and runs `claude plugin validate --strict` + `claude plugin test`; CI gates those two while tsc is machine-local, because the engine writes its declaration only for a session-loaded mod. The id-collision defect their prototype showed (a pane creating records in a checkout colliding with records created on branches) has a create-path counterpart here: the pane's New surface writes a file into the working tree, so it must not offer id allocation that ignores refs.

OPERATOR QUESTIONS, none decided (route to opum-agent as A/Bs when reached; never decide locally; never ask in-pane): (1) body editing — external editor vs in-pane editor vs Claude-assisted only; (2) fleet view — reading other repositories' bundles through a Lore workspace manifest (opum-family currently fails to load because one member does not validate); (3) one mod or two — separate mods per plugin (current direction) vs one Opum workspace pane hosting both.

LIMITS. The release and any registry publication are tier 3, through this session's own dialog. No restart or rollout of the session (OPAG-1069 holds).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The opum-lore plugin ships a hooks module registered from hooks/hooks.json; `claude plugin validate --strict` passes against a stage of exactly the plugin's shipped files, and the module registers a lore command that opens the pane.

Browse and Read: the pane lists the repository bundle's concepts from `lore query` and opens one rendered as Markdown from `lore read`; internal link clicks navigate in the pane with a working Back; a Raw toggle shows the source file including frontmatter.
Search: free text with type and tag filters runs `lore query` and opens results in Read; the include-open-PRs toggle uses `--across-refs`.
New: creates a document through `lore new` from the `lore types` vocabulary with title, summary and tags, and opens the result showing the type's required sections.

Edit, in the session's own repository only: the fields form rewrites frontmatter then validates the written file with `lore validate`, surfacing Lore's own message and keeping the previous file when validation fails; structural operations (rename, supersede, task link/unlink) run the matching lore command and then `lore sync`.
Body editing ships the arm the operator selects when Q1 is routed to opum-agent before implementation, covered by the module's tests.

scripts/mod-test.mjs stages the plugin's shipped files, runs `claude plugin validate --strict` and `claude plugin test`, and reports the typecheck state honestly (machine-local tsc against the engine's declaration; NOT TYPECHECKED rather than implied-green when none exists); CI runs it on PRs.

The operator's answered design questions are recorded through lore as ADRs under this task, their answers verbatim once relayed; the module's own design choices are recorded in a Reference doc and on this record; `lore check` exits 0 and `bun test` passes on the landing branch.

The release carrying the module is tagged and published through the repository's normal release path (tier 3, via this session's own dialog), after the Q3 A/B is relayed and answered; opum-agent is then told so the marketplace pin move can be dispatched.

THE LIBRARY REPORT, carried here because the recycle notice requires it (also in ADR-0026's Decision section):
- Runtime, measured on Claude Code 2.1.287 with probes run through the engine: a bare specifier is refused in the validator's own words ("a hooks module imports its own files by relative path and \"claude-code\", nothing else"); a vendored file imported by relative path is accepted; a file touching `document` stops the module loading ("no DOM in this runtime"); one touching `process`/`require` says "no Node in this runtime". Nothing is installable, and only DOM-free, Node-free source can be vendored.
- The pick: Markdown rendering, diffing and syntax highlighting use the ENGINE'S OWN elements — `Markdown`, and `Code` with `language` and `format: 'diff'` — so no library is vendored for any of the three. The editing model is vendored `@codemirror/state` 6.7.6 plus its one dependency `@marijn/find-cluster-break` 1.0.4: DOM editors (CodeMirror's view, Monaco, ProseMirror) are excluded by the no-DOM measurement and Node TUIs by the no-Node one, and this pair is DOM-free by design, giving grapheme-cluster-correct cursor arithmetic.
- The approved lightweight boundary, as the orchestrator accepted it: text, cursor, insert/delete and undo/redo inside a `Client` region, saving through the shared `lore validate` path with failures restoring the previous bytes; NO highlighting while typing, NO multi-cursor, NO in-editor search; do not add highlight.js or Prism.
- Vendoring conditions, all met: `hooks/vendor/README.md` records each file's package, version, license and sha256, and the ONE rewritten import specifier as a patch with both the upstream and the vendored digests; each license text ships beside its file (`LICENSE-codemirror-state.txt`, `LICENSE-find-cluster-break.txt`); both MIT, both permitting redistribution in this public package.

REVIEWER OUTCOME. A reviewer pass over hooks/editor.tsx, hooks/editor-ops.ts, hooks/vendor/ and the editor wiring in register.tsx -- the arm added after the previous pass and never reviewed -- returned seven findings and answered "do not land". Six were defects; the seventh was three comments that did not describe its code. All are fixed, each with a regression test that reddens on the pre-fix code.

F1 -- SILENT CROSS-DOCUMENT BODY OVERWRITE (the worst of them, and one this session had missed). loadConcept never closed the open body editor, and openConcept only patches the view. Open doc A, edit its body, Browse, open doc B, Save body: saveBody paired doc B's `concept.raw` with doc A's `bodyText` and wrote A's body into B's file -- B's own body destroyed, B's frontmatter kept, so it still validated and the pane still said "Saved and validated." Unrecoverable without git and invisible when it happens. Fixed by binding the editor to a document: `edits` carries `bodyDocId`, loadConcept closes the editor when the document changes, and saveBody refuses when the two disagree.

F2 -- THE SPACE BAR TYPED THE WORD "space". The engine delivers the space bar as the NAME "space", not as the character; the engine's dispatch that builds a Client's key event is `Jr.find(([m]) => i[m])?.[1] ?? (o === " " ? "space" : o)`, read out of the 2.1.287 binary. The printable-key heuristic accepted any name of eight characters or fewer, so the name went into the body -- on the most common keystroke in prose. Fixed: a key is text only when it is a single character, with "space" handled by name.

F3 -- ARROW KEYS AT EITHER END OF THE DOCUMENT THREW. moveCursor called `doc.line(number +/- 1)` unguarded and the vendored `Text.line` throws out of range. editorCreate opens with the cursor on the LAST line, so the first Down press after opening threw, and the engine answers a throw in a Client's key listener by unmounting the instance and never remounting it in place. Clamped.

F4 -- A BODY PAST THE ENGINE'S PROPS BOUND REFUSED THE WHOLE PANE. The pane hands the editor the WHOLE body as Client props, and the engine bounds props and tree at 100,000 characters. Past it the engine reports "opum-lore drew nothing on the terminal surface: ui.render (Pane) refused" -- every control in the pane stops drawing, including the Cancel that would close the editor, so the pane cannot be escaped in place. REACHABLE HERE, not hypothetical: docs/runbooks/release-publishing.md carries a 108,718-character body, docs/reference/lore-cli-release-truth.md 102,239, and docs/reference/cli-surface.md 99,311 (measured with `lore read <id> --json` on this checkout). Fixed with two guards: beginBodyEdit refuses to open on a body it cannot hand back, and the ui.message receiver closes the editor if a body GROWS past the bound. Each points at Open in editor, which has no such bound. A single line past the 10,000-character Text-child bound is refused for the same reason.

F5 -- THE EDITOR DREW A ONE-LINE WINDOW. The Client element carried no height, and a Client with none is "as tall as what the module draws" while the module draws one row fewer than its region: a region sized by its own content, whose only fixed point is a single visible document line. Given an explicit height.

F6 -- BACKSPACE AT A LINE'S START AND DELETE AT A LINE'S END WERE NO-OPs THAT ATE THE REDO RING. The line break is not part of `line.text`, so the cluster walk found nothing and the change range came out empty: the text did not change, but a new state object still went onto the undo ring and dropped the redo ring with it. Both now join the lines, and `edited()` refuses a state whose document is unchanged.

F7 (minor) -- saveBody's failure path bumped bodyRevision, which re-created the editor from the text it already held: a cursor jump to the end and a discarded redo ring, not the "revert after a failed save" three comments claimed. The bump is gone and the comments corrected.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, because a checked box stops anyone else looking. Every new case was mutation-checked by restoring its own defect: the arrow-key guard, the space branch, both line-join directions, the height, and both size guards each reddened EXACTLY the one test written for it, the rest staying green. Two honest exceptions. The cross-document close is defended twice, so removing either guard alone leaves the suite green -- only removing both reddens its test, which therefore pins the behaviour rather than either guard. And removing either size guard reddens its test with the engine's own words in the output ("drew nothing on the terminal surface: ui.render (Pane) refused"), which is this session's own reproduction of F4's blast radius rather than a relay of the reviewer's.

A CORRECTION THIS SESSION OWES. This session first REFUTED the space-bar defect, reasoning from the engine's TypeScript declaration ("or the character typed"). The declaration's list is illustrative and its ellipsis hides "space"; the reviewer read the binary, and this session then confirmed it in the binary directly. The refutation was wrong and is recorded here so it is not re-derived. The lesson is the fleet's own: an inference from prose is not a measurement, and the producing artifact beats a summary of it.
